title: cold-start-sequence-k8s-rollback-exercises-baremetal-vsphere-notes
content:
Purpose This is a working sketch for a ‘cold start’ and rollback rehearsal plan covering both bare‑metal and vSphere private clusters. The goal: define a repeatable exercise for rebuilding a cluster from infrastructure + etcd snapshots, verify app-level recovery, and validate Terraform lifecycle hooks we rely on for private deployment automation. Context and motivation - We regularly exercise node rotation and rolling upgrades, but we have fewer rehearsals that start from an empty facility / destroyed control plane and require full rebuild. - Two common customer asks: (1) ability to reprovision a customer VPC/on‑prem cluster quickly from committed infra + snapshot, (2) confidence the Terraform modules perform a clean teardown/recreate path. - This doc mixes ops runbook steps with notes for Terraform module improvements and a list of test cases for the chaos/DR exercise. Glossary / assumptions - control plane = kube-apiserver + controller-manager + scheduler + etcd cluster (3 nodes typical). - worker plane = application nodes and GPU nodes. - etcd snapshot = etcdctl snapshot taken with TLS creds, stored in object store (S3/GCS) or on a recovery USB for airgap runs. - Terraform hooks = CLI scripts invoked in module lifecycle (pre-apply, post-apply, pre-destroy). High level steps for cold start rehearsal (happy path) 1) Prepare test bed - Select a lab rack or vSphere test cluster. Label it as CHALLENGE-A.
- Ensure access keys in credential manager (vault path: secret/infra/challenge-a) are valid. - Place etcd snapshot file(s) in recovery bucket: s3://redwood-labs/cold-start/challenge-a/etcd-snap-{timestamp}.db. 2) Wipe existing infra (simulate disaster) - For baremetal: trigger IPMI power off + PXE wipe for all nodes involved. For vSphere: snapshot and then delete the VMs (preserve datastore snapshot if testing partial failure). - Remove any cloud DNS A/AAAA records created by previous runs. 3) Run Terraform apply to create infra base layer - terraform -chdir=./tf/private-deployments challenge-a init && terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan && terraform apply plan.tfplan - Pre-apply hook should: validate VLANs, allocate IP ranges, register hostnames in lab DNS, and upload bootstrap ISO for PXE. 4) Bootstrap control plane nodes - For kubeadm-based installs: run kubeadm init with flags that point to restore from etcd snapshot (kubeadm provides etcd restore docs). If using custom operator, follow operator restore sequence. - After control plane up: verify etcd cluster size, healthy, and restored keys: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/etcd/pki/ca.crt snapshot status /recovery/etcd-snap.db 5) Reattach worker nodes and validate workloads - Workers should join automatically via node join tokens or preseeded kubeconfigs. Validate DaemonSets and GPU plugin come up. - Smoke test: run conformance-like pod that hits internal services and checks model-serving endpoints. 6) Post-checks and metrics - Validate API latency, pod scheduling time, and all storage volumes reattached. Compare with baseline CSV in S3. - Archive logs and the runbook outcome to S3 for audit. Failure modes to rehearse (add as separate iterations) - Etcd partial snapshot: simulate missing a member's WAL files -> observe restore options and required steps to rehydrate missing keys. - Lost control plane certificates: exercise re-issuing certs via CA and rejoin controllers. - Network partition between nodes: simulate by iptables rules and validate operator fallback behaviors. - PVs stuck on nodes that were wiped: test CSI volume re-attach/recover. - Terraform drift: remove resources manually and ensure terraform plan detects and can recreate them safely. Terraform module / lifecycle hook notes (what to improve) - Add an explicit pre-destroy confirmation flag for destructive runs that require human confirmation (TF var: allow_destruction_override). Current behavior is too permissive for lab runs when run by less-senior engineers. - Provide an option to create ephemeral DNS zones per run; makes simultaneous exercises less noisy. (module: dns/ephemeral_zone boolean). - Hook for post-apply: run a verification script that returns machine-level health, and fail the Terraform apply if basic provisioning failed. This reduces silent failures. - Introduce a ‘recovery-mode’ path that skips creating worker VMs and only brings up control plane for faster iteration. (TF flag: recovery_only). - Record the Terraform state 'run-id' as a tag on VMs and datastore objects to make destroy easier when multiple runs coexist. Validation checklist (to gate graduation of the exercise) - [ ] Control plane healthy (kube-system pods all running) - [ ] etcd snapshot restored and leader elected - [ ] Nodes able to schedule test workload (NGINX + model server) - [ ] Ingress/loadbalancer reachable from external test harness - [ ] No manual secret copy steps required beyond documented steps - [ ] Terraform plan after run shows no unintended drifts - [ ] Postmortem created and linked in JIRA ticket Commands & snippets (examples) - Upload etcd snapshot to S3: aws s3 cp /tmp/etcd-snap.db s3://redwood-labs/cold-start/challenge-a/ --acl private - Check etcd snapshot: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot status /tmp/etcd-snap.db --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/etcd/pki/ca.crt - Terraform apply with run-id: TF_VAR_run_id=challenge-a-202503 terraform apply -var='run_id=challenge-a-202503' Runbook play-by-play (example timeline for a single 4‑hour drill) - 00:00–00:30: Kickoff, confirm vault creds, and ensure recovery snapshot available. - 00:30–01:00: Lab operator wipes/isolates nodes (or delete vSphere VMs). - 01:00–01:30: terraform apply base infra (network, DNS, datastore). - 01:30–02:00: Bootstrap control plane and run etcd restore. - 02:00–02:45: Attach workers and validate workload scheduling. - 02:45–03:15: Run failure scenarios (network partition, volume detachment). - 03:15–03:45: Run terraform destroy and confirm clean up. - 03:45–04:00: Postmortem notes and capture lessons. Postmortem template (what to capture) - start_timestamp, end_timestamp, lead_operator, unexpected_blockers, time_to_restore_control_plane, time_to_recover_app, terraform_issues, remediation_actions, owners_for_followups. Open questions / TODOs - Decide canonical location for archived etcd snapshots for exercises vs customer-run backups. (ops question) - Should we integrate a small CI job that runs 'recovery_only' nightly on non-prod hardware? Pros/cons: early catching of infra bitrot vs cost. - How to handle licensing/airgap: include a step to verify that downstream container images are present in local registry and document exact registry import steps. References and links - GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra (PR-764 for tf recovery flags) - Jira: JIRA-INFRA-4287 (cold-start exercise epic) - Confluence: private-deployments/cold-start-runbook (template) Notes for the next iteration (follow ups) - Convert the post-apply verification script into a Kubernetes job that uses kubectl to assert expected objects exist; wire it as a webhook to Terraform. - Add a small chaos script to automatically run the 3 failure modes from above and produce a scorecard. - Draft a shorter ‘run checklist’ play card that fits on a single page for on-call/field ops use. Notes to self - run this exercise with Diego and S. Nguyen next Friday (reserve lab rack). Bring USB copy of latest etcd snapshot in addition to S3. - capture video of the rebuild steps for runbook animation.
